You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

    content='''ARC task-76e1d5d7 TEST-VERIFIED RULE: The grid has two panels separated by a monochrome divider. Align the panels along their shared coordinate (same row for side-by-side panels; same column for stacked panels). Compare each pair of colored symbols. In the MOVING panel, a symbol whose corresponding symbol in the static panel has the SAME color moves to the cell adjacent to the divider; a symbol whose corresponding color DIFFERS moves to the far outer edge of its panel. Clear its original cell. Preserve the static panel, divider, background, and borders.

CRITICAL: Identify which panel moves by symbol placement, not by top/left or panel size. The STATIC/reference panel's symbols are already in the line adjacent to the divider. The MOVING panel's symbols begin farther away from the divider. This applies in either direction: left or right, top or bottom. Demo 7 had a static left panel and moving right panel. Correct test: keep rows 0-5 unchanged; move bottom color 1 at col 7 to row 6 because it matches top col 7; move all six mismatched bottom colors to row 15 at their original columns (col1=2,col3=2,col5=9,col9=8,col11=9,col13=8); clear row 10.

Rejected interpretations: modifying the top/left panel by default is wrong. Do not collapse all mismatches into one edge cell; each retains its aligned column/row. In an earlier wrong top-panel attempt, mismatches were moved to row 0 and the match left at row 4, but this modified the wrong panel. The inverse comparison rule was also wrong.''',

Align the panels along their shared coordinate (same row for side-by-side panels; same column for stacked panels). Compare each pair of colored symbols. In the MOVING panel, a symbol whose corresponding symbol in the static panel has the SAME color moves to the cell adjacent to the divider; a symbol whose corresponding color DIFFERS moves to the far outer edge of its panel. Clear its original cell. Preserve the static panel, divider, background, and borders.

CRITICAL: Identify which panel moves by symbol placement, not by top/left or panel size. The STATIC/reference panel's symbols are already in the line adjacent to the divider. The MOVING panel's symbols begin farther away from the divider. This applies in either direction: left or right, top or bottom. Demo 7 had a static left panel and moving right panel. The 16x16 test had a static TOP panel (symbols at row 4 beside divider row 5) and moving BOTTOM panel (symbols at row 10). Correct test: keep rows 0-5 unchanged; move bottom color 1 at col 7 to row 6 because it matches top col 7; move all six mismatched bottom colors to row 15 at their original columns (col1=2,col3=2,col5=9,col9=8,col11=9,col13=8); clear row 10.

Rejected interpretations: modifying the top/left panel by default is wrong. Do not collapse all mismatches into one edge cell; each retains its aligned column/row. In an earlier wrong top-panel attempt, mismatches were moved to row 0 and the match left at row 4, but this modified the wrong panel. The inverse comparison rule was also wrong.", path='arc/task-76e1d5d7', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-11-08T05:49:44.319785+00:00', updated_at='2026-11-08T05:49:44.319800+00:00', version=1)
